q: Where are users, groups and service principals created in a workspace with identity federation?
o: In each workspace separately
In the account, then assigned to workspaces
In the Unity Catalog metastore
In the cloud provider's IAM console
e: Identities are managed once at the account level and assigned to the workspaces that need them, so one person is one principal everywhere.

q: Why can you not run `GRANT SELECT ... TO finance` when `finance` is a legacy workspace-local group?
o: Workspace-local groups cannot receive Unity Catalog grants
Groups can never receive grants, only users can
The group name needs backticks
Only service principals can get SELECT
e: Unity Catalog serves many workspaces, so it only knows account-level groups. Convert the group to an account group.

q: A nightly Lakeflow Job loads production data. Which setup is best?
o: Run as the data engineer who built it
Run as a workspace admin
Use a personal access token of a team lead
Run as a service principal that authenticates with OAuth
e: A service principal outlives any person, holds only the grants the job needs, and OAuth M2M gives short-lived tokens instead of a long-lived personal token.

q: What does `is_account_group_member('data-engineers')` return for a user who is in `team-a`, which is itself a member of `data-engineers`?
o: false, only direct membership counts
An error, because nested groups are not supported
true, because indirect membership counts
NULL
e: The function returns true for direct or indirect members of an account group, so nested membership counts.

q: A user is assigned to a workspace but cannot open the SQL editor. What is the most likely cause?
o: They lack the Databricks SQL access entitlement
They are not a metastore admin
They have no USE CATALOG grant
They are not in the `account users` group
e: Entitlements decide which parts of a workspace a principal may use. The SQL editor and warehouses need Databricks SQL access.
